steps.phase: Define clients, trust boundaries, and cross-modal context
steps.title: Translate the brief into latency classes and trust boundaries
steps.content: The brief requires text, image, audio, and video input; cross-modal reasoning; text/image/audio generation; persistent cross-modal conversation context; tool calling; PDF/chart understanding; real-time voice; and safety across every modality. Clarify whether 'text response under 1 second' means first token or a complete response; provisionally define it as p95 time-to-first-meaningful-token across every accepted text turn, including cold-route and retrieval cases, and measure full completion separately. Apply the under-2-second p95 target to initial global understanding for every accepted single-image input up to 100MB, measured after upload completes; use parallel multi-scale inference and reserved capacity rather than excluding high-resolution images. Full PDF/video extraction and deeper follow-up analysis can continue asynchronously after the initial response. Stream voice.

steps.content: The orchestrator owns the product's modality workflow while the AI Gateway isolates model vendors. Persist references and versioned representations rather than provider-specific session IDs as the source of truth. steps.content: Every accepted text turn and single-image request takes the low-latency interactive path: stream text, and use bounded parallel multi-scale inference to return initial global image understanding within the 2-second target after upload completes. Audio voice uses streaming chunks and partial transcripts. steps.content: Conversation state is ordered in the durable store; hot summaries are only a cache. steps.phase: Ground answers and preserve cross-modal conversation state
steps.title: Define latency as measurable service targets
steps.content: Define the brief's text target as p95 time-to-first-meaningful-token under 1s across every accepted text turn, including cold-route and retrieval cases. Require p95 initial global understanding under 2s for every accepted single-image input up to 100MB, measured after upload completion; use reserved low-latency capacity and parallel multi-scale inference, with no warm-only or compact-image-only exception. Measure full long-form generation separately; video and multipage-document extraction may continue asynchronously after the initial response.

decision.question: Define latency as measurable service targets
decision.chosen: Meet under 1s p95 to first meaningful text token for every accepted text turn and under 2s p95 initial understanding for every accepted single-image input up to 100MB; continue only secondary document/video enrichment asynchronously.
decision.chosenReason: The latency constraints apply across accepted text and image traffic, not only warm or compact subsets. Reserved inference capacity and parallel multi-scale processing protect the first response; upload transfer and full long-form completion are measured separately.

properties.purpose: Manage turn state and modality routing with explicit p95 budgets across all accepted traffic: under 1s to first meaningful text token for every text turn, including cold-route and retrieval cases; under 2s initial global understanding for every accepted single-image input up to 100MB after upload, using reserved capacity and parallel multi-scale inference; and real-time voice. Queue only full video/multipage-document extraction or deeper enrichment after the initial response, not high-resolution images as a class.

steps.phase: Generate safely, call tools under authorization, and operate the service
steps.title: Use explicit confirmation for high-impact tool calls
steps.content: Read-only and low-risk functions can execute within a narrow grant. Sending messages, changing permissions, deleting data, or spending money requires a user confirmation step; retries use an idempotency key so a timeout cannot duplicate an external action.

decision.question: Use explicit confirmation for high-impact tool calls
decision.chosen: Re-authorize every allowlisted tool call; execute with least privilege, timeout, and idempotency; require explicit user confirmation for destructive, externally visible, permission-changing, or financial actions.
decision.chosenReason: Read-only and low-risk functions can execute within a narrow grant. Sending messages, changing permissions, deleting data, or spending money requires a user confirmation step; retries use an idempotency key so a timeout cannot duplicate an external action.

properties.purpose: Re-authorize every allowlisted tool call; execute with least privilege, timeout, and idempotency; require explicit user confirmation for destructive, externally visible, permission-changing, or financial actions.

steps.phase: Generate safely, call tools under authorization, and operate the service
steps.title: Make language, media size, and failure behavior visible
steps.content: Advertise the actually supported 50+ languages per modality and fall back clearly when a speech model lacks one. Show upload progress for files up to 100MB, retry resumable chunks, and report extraction failures with the page/frame that failed. On provider outage, preserve the user's turn, return partial streamed work when safe, and offer a retry or async completion rather than a confident empty answer.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Route work by remaining deadline, not a single hard-coded file-size cutoff
steps.content: Keep a turn synchronous only when its estimated preprocessing, retrieval, model, and guardrail work fits the remaining modality-specific response budget. Route video, large PDFs, or any job projected to exceed that budget to the durable queue; let the text/voice conversation continue with a clearly labeled partial result and job status. The 100MB limit is an admission ceiling, not a promise of interactive processing. Configure thresholds from measured p95 data and keep source/page/time provenance on partial results.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Choose the sync-versus-async policy
steps.content: Keep every accepted text turn and single-image request on the interactive first-response path: pre-provision text inference and run parallel multi-scale image inference to meet the measured p95 targets. Route video and multipage-document extraction, plus deeper follow-up enrichment, to the durable queue without delaying the initial answer. Return a labeled partial/pending state for those secondary jobs; never claim unfinished extraction is complete. Resumable upload is capped at 100MB, and the image-processing clock starts after upload completes.

decision.question: How should the orchestrator route mixed quick prompts and heavy media?
decision.chosen: Serve the first meaningful response for every accepted text turn and single-image input within their p95 targets; queue only secondary video/document extraction and deeper enrichment.
decision.chosenReason: The brief does not exempt cold text turns or high-resolution images from its latency targets. Reserved capacity and parallel multi-scale inference handle the first response; long-form extraction can continue with explicit progress afterward.

alternatives.option: Always process all attached media synchronously
alternatives.tradeoff: A large file can block a quick text or voice response and violate the interactive target.

properties.purpose: Manage modality routing with explicit deadlines across all accepted traffic: p95 under 1s to first meaningful text token for every text turn, including cold-route and retrieval cases; p95 under 2s initial global understanding for every accepted single-image input up to 100MB after upload, using reserved capacity and parallel multi-scale inference; and streaming voice. Do not exclude high-resolution images or warm-only routes. Queue full video/multipage-document extraction and deeper enrichment only after the initial answer. For real-time voice, allow one same-capability failover within the remaining deadline; if still late, close with retryable VOICE_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and safe partial transcript/audio state.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Keep multilingual failover capability-equivalent
steps.content: At turn start, choose a primary provider only if it supports the requested language, modality, safety policy, streaming mode, and quality floor. On timeout or outage, fail over to an approved provider with the same capability contract; if none is available, degrade explicitly (for example, offer a transcript/text path or async retry) rather than silently switch to unsupported speech. Pin provider behavior for a turn unless failing over, preserve locale/output format, keep product-owned conversation state, and run the same input/output guardrails on every route.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Choose capability-gated multilingual provider fallback
steps.content: Use a versioned, ordered route table: the configured primary first, then the first enabled fallback with the same language, modality, streaming, policy, and quality capabilities. Permit at most one transparent failover per turn and pin the selected route for the rest of that turn. If a matching async route exists, return 202 with status=queued and a jobId; otherwise terminate the stream with a retryable CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE or LATENCY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED event and any explicitly marked safe partial output. Never silently switch language, modality, or policy.

decision.question: What should happen when the selected ASR/TTS/model provider misses its SLO?
decision.chosen: Fail over only to an approved provider meeting the same language, modality, policy, and streaming contract; otherwise degrade explicitly.
decision.chosenReason: A deterministic priority list avoids route oscillation; at most one compatible failover preserves behavior. If no route qualifies, a typed queued/degraded response is safer than silently using an unsupported provider.

alternatives.option: Retry against any available model provider
alternatives.tradeoff: The fallback may not support the requested language, modality, latency, or policy.

properties.purpose: Select providers from a versioned deterministic route table per required language, modality, streaming mode, policy, and quality floor: configured primary, then the first enabled exact-capability fallback by explicit priority. Allow at most one transparent failover and pin the route for the rest of a turn. Never switch language/modality/policy silently. If no eligible provider meets the remaining deadline, return 202 {status:queued,jobId} only when a matching async route exists; otherwise emit a terminal retryable {code:CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE or LATENCY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED,partialAvailable:boolean} result.

steps.title: Turn “50+ languages” into a release-tested capability contract
steps.content: Count distinct language identifiers, not regional variants twice. A locale counts only when text input/output and real-time streaming ASR/TTS work end to end, the same safety policy runs, measured text/voice latency meets the brief, and a capability-equivalent fallback is qualified. Keep a versioned provider/model matrix with last-pass test evidence; block rollout and remove any unsupported language claim if fewer than 50 qualify.
steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Add the versioned language capability registry
steps.content: Store one qualified row per language/provider/model route: BCP-47 tag and base language, text input/output, streaming ASR/TTS, safety profile, primary/fallback priority, text first-token and voice streaming measurements, model version, test-suite revision, and qualification timestamp. Count distinct base languages only when all required modality and latency checks pass; enforce at least 50.

component.label: Versioned Language Capability Registry
component.description: Qualified language, modality, fallback, and SLO matrix

properties.purpose: Maintain versioned per-language/provider/model qualification rows for text input/output, streaming ASR/TTS, safety, primary/fallback priority, measured latency, model version, and test evidence. Release predicate: at least 50 distinct base languages pass the full text+streaming-speech and safety/SLO suite; regional aliases never count twice.

component.highlightReason: The 50+ language requirement must be measured per modality, latency, and safety—not inferred from a provider marketing label.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Require a verified language route before a turn starts
steps.content: Resolve the requested or detected language against the qualified matrix before routing. Return only providers/models that passed the exact text or speech capability and current safety/SLO gate.

connection.label: Verified language capability lookup
connection.description: Resolve language, modality, safety, latency, and approved fallback from the qualified route matrix before model selection.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Return the qualified primary and fallback routes
steps.content: The registry returns a versioned capability decision to the AI Gateway. If a requested language/modality lacks an approved route, do not silently substitute another language; return the typed unsupported/degraded result defined in the gateway policy.

connection.label: Qualified route manifest
connection.description: Return the approved language-specific primary/fallback set, capability version, and latest test/SLO status.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Make 50+ full-pipeline languages a release invariant
steps.content: Before launch or a model/provider change, count distinct base languages with passing text input/output, streaming ASR/TTS, safety, required latency, and equivalent fallback tests. Release only when at least 50 meet the whole contract; otherwise fail the gate and do not claim 50+ support. At runtime, use only that qualified set.

decision.question: How do you prevent an unverified provider claim from counting as 50+ language support?
decision.chosen: Require at least 50 distinct languages to pass text, streaming speech, safety, SLO, and fallback tests before release.
decision.chosenReason: The registry makes the published capability measurable and prevents locale aliases or batch-only speech from inflating coverage.

alternatives.option: Trust a provider’s general language list
alternatives.tradeoff: A listed language may lack streaming speech, safety coverage, latency, or a qualified fallback.

properties.purpose: Select providers only from the versioned qualified language registry. Release is blocked unless at least 50 distinct base languages pass text input/output, real-time streaming ASR/TTS, safety, latency, and equivalent-fallback tests; regional variants do not count twice. At runtime use configured primary then first exact-capability fallback, at most one failover; never silently change language/modality, and return the typed queued/degraded result when no route qualifies.

steps.title: Add the policy and content-change event bus
steps.content: Publish consent changes, retention changes, document edits, access revocations, and deletion/tombstone events with tenant, entity ID, monotonic version, event ID, and retention deadline. Consumers deduplicate and ignore stale versions; access checks fail closed immediately while asynchronous cache/index/object cleanup catches up.

component.label: Consent & Content Invalidation Bus
component.description: Versioned policy, edit, and deletion events

properties.purpose: Durably fan out tenant-scoped consent, retention, edit, revocation, and deletion events with monotonic entity versions and idempotent event IDs; consumers reject stale events, retry boundedly, and expose lag.

component.highlightReason: Consent and deletion must propagate through derived context and media, not stop at the auth or source-store boundary.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Publish authorization and consent changes
steps.content: The policy service emits permission/consent revocations and retention-policy changes. Retrieval and cached-context reads fail closed as soon as the authoritative policy version advances, even before cleanup finishes.

connection.label: Consent / access policy change
connection.description: Publish tenant-scoped, versioned consent grants/revocations and retention updates.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Publish conversation and document mutations
steps.content: Committed edits, explicit user deletions, and tombstones flow from the source-of-truth store. Stable event IDs and entity revisions make replay idempotent and prevent older events from resurrecting removed context.

connection.label: Edit / delete / retention event
connection.description: Publish committed conversation and artifact revisions, tombstones, and retention expirations.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Invalidate hot summaries and intermediate representations
steps.content: The cache consumer advances a tenant/entity generation, removes prior summary and derived-representation keys, and rejects delayed writes from older turns. In-flight reads compare policy/entity versions before returning data.

connection.label: Versioned context invalidation
connection.description: Advance cache generations and remove stale summaries/representations idempotently.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Tombstone or remove revoked retrieval evidence
steps.content: The index consumer applies version-checked tombstones to document chunks and captions. Every query still checks current tenant permissions, so eventual physical deletion never becomes temporary unauthorized disclosure.

connection.label: Retrieval tombstone / access update
connection.description: Version-check and delete or tombstone affected embeddings and source chunks; enforce current access filters at read time.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Apply media retention and deletion to stored objects
steps.content: A bounded idempotent consumer deletes expired/revoked source objects and derived artifacts, then records completion or retry state. The conversation store retains only the policy-allowed tombstone/audit record.

connection.label: Media retention / object deletion
connection.description: Apply versioned retention and deletion to source media and derived artifacts with retryable completion state.

steps.title: Cancel queued work after revocation
steps.content: Advance or cancel matching jobs by tenant and entity generation. Queued consumers recheck the authoritative generation before processing; retries cannot revive an older job.

connection.label: Cancel stale media jobs
connection.description: Cancel or supersede queued jobs by tenant/entity generation; consumers recheck current policy before start.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Stop in-flight preprocessing and reject stale outputs
steps.content: Cancellation is cooperative at each stage boundary. After OCR, ASR, frame extraction, or external model calls, a worker performs a version-checked conditional commit; if the policy generation changed, it discards the result and emits no embedding or artifact.

connection.label: Cancel / reject stale worker output
connection.description: Propagate policy generations to workers; cancel work and require version-checked commit before publishing derived output.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Cancel active turns and revoke pending responses
steps.content: On access revocation or deletion, stop affected live streams, invalidate pending tool/model continuations, and prevent a late partial response from being delivered under the old authorization version.

connection.label: Cancel active turn / response
connection.description: Stop active turns and suppress late model/tool responses whose policy generation is no longer current.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps

steps.title: Choose commit-time policy-version checks
steps.content: Every async worker and retrieval/artifact publisher carries the tenant/entity policy generation from job admission. Recheck before each sensitive read and conditionally commit only if authorization and source version still match. A revocation cancels queue work, interrupts active turns, fails closed on reads, and discards late outputs.

decision.question: How do you prevent an in-flight job from recreating deleted or revoked context?
decision.chosen: Cancel queued/active work and require an authoritative generation match at every read and conditional output commit.
decision.chosenReason: Event delivery is at-least-once and can race with worker output; a commit-time version check makes late work harmless even if cancellation arrives late.

alternatives.option: Rely only on eventual cache/index deletion events
alternatives.tradeoff: A late OCR/embedding/model result can repopulate data after deletion.

properties.purpose: Run modality-specific normalization with tenant policy generation and source revision carried on every job. Recheck authorization before sensitive reads and at each output commit; cancel queued/in-flight work on revocation, conditionally commit only if the authoritative generation/source version still matches, and discard stale OCR/ASR/frame/vector/artifact outputs.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Choose fail-closed, versioned invalidation
steps.content: Advance the authoritative generation first; reject stale cache/index reads immediately, then asynchronously and idempotently erase derived representations and media. Track queue lag and deletion completion so the system can prove when cleanup is done.

decision.question: How do consent revocation and deletion reach every derived copy?
decision.chosen: Emit versioned events from policy and source stores; fail closed on reads immediately and clean cache, retrieval, and media asynchronously.
decision.chosenReason: This separates immediate authorization safety from slower physical deletion while making replay and completion auditable.

alternatives.option: Delete only from the conversation store
alternatives.tradeoff: Cached summaries, embeddings, or media artifacts could remain visible or be reused.

properties.purpose: Cache versioned conversation summaries and intermediate representations with tenant-scoped keys, bounded TTL, and policy/entity generations. On consent, access, edit, retention, or deletion events, reject stale reads immediately, advance generation, and idempotently remove derived values; ignore delayed writes from older versions.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Measure completion and degradation as product behavior
steps.content: Expose per-modality p50/p95 first-token or understanding time, full response time, async job age, fallback/degraded rate by supported language, invalidation lag, and deletion completion. Keep raw prompt/media out of telemetry by default; use sampled, consented diagnostics for quality investigations.

steps.phase: Close provider, language, and invalidation gaps
steps.title: Review the end-to-end design against the brief
steps.content: The design supports all four input modalities, cross-modal reasoning, text/image/audio generation, persistent context, constrained tools, PDF/chart extraction, streaming voice, and modality-wide safety. Text and voice routes are contract-tested across at least 50 distinct languages before release; unsupported routes are never silently claimed. Interactive SLOs are explicit and provisional where the brief is ambiguous; expensive media uses deadline-aware asynchronous work; and versioned events plus commit-time checks stop revoked/deleted data from reappearing.
